evidence:
Reviewed the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A34:D34 is check 33, requiring ONE full-credit bar and reporting descriptions that enumerate requirements then waive them. Internal Quality Checks!E34 says multiple verifiers may be combined into one flow to avoid retesting. Applied the frozen Harbor SKILL.md Known false positives section and references/quality-checks.md:138-140, while applying qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md's independent-outcome correction. This does not treat multi-step evidence collection as a defect by itself.

Complete inventory: parsed and individually read all five frozen tests/*/*/judge.toml files: Render 1 binary criterion, Constraints 1 binary criterion, Functional 64 binary criteria, Polish 7 binary criteria, Visual 6 five-point criteria: 79 total, all nonempty descriptions. Read all five associated prompts and the injected tests/app_context.md as well as the public brief and all six operating notes. No criterion was found to demand one full-credit result and then allow a materially weaker result for that same outcome. All 84 frozen task/rules hashes independently recomputed against qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/manifest.json matched; input_sha256 agrees with the assigned snapshot.

Concrete consistency checks (task-relative citations refer to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/): gates/render/judge.toml:23-27 requires an actual authored preview AND console marker; its final limitation to an ordinary successful run does not waive either marker. gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 requires a successful new save and exact record retrieval in a clean context and after reload; excluding SQLite-specific proof, revisions and restart does not replace that shared-write/read bar with a health-only bar. Functional prompt.md:100 expressly says shared controls are facts, not sibling pass prerequisites, and cannot establish protection merely from absence. Functional judge.toml:49/63 separates ordinary filename dispatch from extension case; prompt.md:143 permits lowercase fallback only for the former. Functional judge.toml:77 retains actual control-script and handler markers, an enabled retained button and an ordinary successful browser click for inert copying; exempting CSS colour does not waive any inert-copy requirement. Functional judge.toml:294/301 explicitly requires an observed automatic execution before off-state suppression; only correct debounce-reset behavior is excluded as a sibling outcome. Functional judge.toml:350/357 and prompt.md:411-415 maintain separate restart readback and post-restart write outcomes; the fresh-record fallback is expressly for writing and cannot earn old-record survival. Functional judge.toml:371 and prompt.md:421-425 allow proactive conflict prevention only with useful feedback, exact dirty-field preservation and deliberate latest-revision recovery, plus a separate server-refusal observation. Functional judge.toml:119/427 permits hidden provisional candidates while still requiring the last-good completed render; public behaviour.md:13 explicitly allows provisional rendering and static rollback.

Polish judge.toml:23 requires all three panes usable at mobile size while allowing tabs/stacking and horizontal code scrolling; these are implementation alternatives, not a waiver of access. Polish judge.toml:50 requires visible focus for reached controls, explicitly requires some positive keyboard focus evidence, and leaves reachability to its own row. Polish judge.toml:68 asks for one ordinary supported action from the outset; it does not first demand every action then waive most. Visual judge.toml:25,40,55,70,85 each has one full-credit anchor; simple/native styling and minor harmless imperfections remain compatible with the stated readable/coherent target. Visual judge.toml:99-104 consistently assigns composition across widths to Visual and operability/clipping/overflow to Polish, matching visual/prompt.md:17-22.

Adversarial source walkthroughs: (1) A conforming implementation that proactively disables stale Save with clear conflict feedback, preserves every dirty field, permits ordinary latest-version reload/reapply, and rejects a replayed old revision fits the explicit alternative; it is not falsely failed for lacking a forced click or special Restore button. (2) A broken app that implements manual Run but never executes any automatic edit cannot earn off-state suppression merely by staying silent: Functional judge.toml:294/301 and prompt.md:379 explicitly fail that absence-only witness. (3) A CSS implementation that removes/hides/disables the retained control instead of isolating its old handler cannot earn inert-copy credit under judge.toml:77 and prompt.md:137. (4) A database that loses old records on restart yet permits fresh writes can earn only the write outcome through the stated fallback, not durability. None exposes two conflicting full-credit targets. These were logical contract walkthroughs, not executed alternate apps.

This result establishes only row 33's source-level consistency. The raw-evidence-index limitation states that full configured verifier, Oracle, target-model and measured judge workload evidence is absent. No runtime result or score is inferred, no paid/network/Docker runs were made, and no peer or previous reviewer verdict was consulted.
